title: Write a constrained template
summary: Turn an int-only clamp into a template and explain instantiation errors.

scenario.briefing: A clamp helper works only for int, so telemetry code duplicates it for doubles. Generalize it with a type parameter and keep both bounds correct.

objectives.description: Write a function template that handles both bounds.
Explain where template errors appear and why.
Explain instantiation, concepts, and header definitions accurately.

hints: Replace every int in the signature with the type parameter.
Declare template <typename T> before the function.
Check the low bound first and the high bound second.
Return low when value is below low, high when above high, otherwise value.

misconceptions.description: Leaving the helper typed as int.
misconceptions.testDescription: The template is declared with a type parameter.
misconceptions.feedback: A single int signature forces callers to convert or duplicate. Use template <typename T> and T for the value and bounds.
Templates are instantiated at compile time. The compiler generates a concrete function for each used type.

misconceptions.description: Putting a template definition in a .cpp file.
misconceptions.feedback: Other translation units cannot see the body, so instantiation fails at link time. Keep template definitions in headers.

sections.title: A template is a compile-time pattern
sections.body: A function template declares a type parameter, and the compiler generates a concrete function for each type used at a call site. The generated code is checked when it is instantiated, which is why a template error often points at the caller rather than the template definition.

sections.title: Constraints express requirements
sections.body: A template that uses comparison operators requires a type that supports those operators. C++20 concepts such as std::totally_ordered state the requirement in the signature. Constraints improve error messages and prevent accidental instantiations.

sections.title: Definitions belong in headers
sections.body: The compiler needs the template body at the point of instantiation. Putting a template definition in a .cpp file usually produces a link error because other translation units cannot see it. Keep templates in headers or explicitly instantiate them.

steps.title: Generalize clamp
steps.prompt: Edit main.cpp. clamp_value is a function template that returns low when value is below low, high when value is above high, and value otherwise.

localVerification.description: Compile main.cpp with the C++20 standard.

tests.description: The template is declared with a type parameter.
includes: T clamp_value(T value, T low, T high)

tests.description: The helper remains usable with doubles.

hints: The signature repeats int three times.
Add a template parameter before the return type.
Use T for value, low, and high.
Add a double call in main to prove the second instantiation.

steps.title: Where does the error appear?
steps.prompt: A template uses operator< but is called with a type that does not define it. Where does the compiler usually report the problem?

options.label: At the call site that instantiates the template
At runtime, when the operator is executed
Only in the linker, after every translation unit compiles

quiz.explanation: The template body is checked when the compiler instantiates it for a concrete type. The diagnostic often points into the template but is triggered by the call.
